best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Fusion DMG% boost and an additional 30% Fusion DMG% after using a Resonance Skill for a grand total of 40% additional Fusion damage. On Encore, if using her standard rotation, make sure to cast a Resonance Skill right before casting Ultimate (you can cancel it instantly to save time while still activating the effect!)

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Fusion DMG and 12% Resonance Skill DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Fusion focused resonators who emphasize Resonance Skill damage. While Resonance Skill damage isn't Encore's main damage type, it does provide a solid enough boost to warrant usage due to how easy it is to activate this Echo skill comparatively to the non-nightmare variant.

Gives a 12% Basic Attack DMG bonus and 12% Fusion DMG bonus after being transformed into and its last of 3 hits was dealt, for a duration of 15 seconds. This makes this Echo preferable for characters who prefer Basic DMG over Skill DMG, but this option is more difficult to incorporate in rotations than the Nightmare variant, often requiring Swap Cancelling to be smooth. Still Encore's best choice overall if you can manage it properly.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Increases Fusion DMG Bonus by 10% unconditionally and gives all party members 15% Fusion DMG Bonus when casting Ultimate on top of giving the equipper 20% Liberation DMG Bonus, all of these effects lasting 35s (which means they can be permanently applicable if maintained). Note that this effect does not stack if running the set multiple times in the same team. Not optimal on Encore in her best teams, but definitely worth using in a Dual DPS team with Changli or Brant to also increase their damage. Note that this set forces Encore into using her Ultimate-enhanced Forte Heavy Attack due to boosting Liberation damage significantly.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Increases Liberation and Fusion damage by 12% when equipped in the Main Slot, a simple Summon Echo that deals damage and doesn't cost any time or have any condition on the cast. The best and only option that the Flaming Clawprint Echo set has.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Calculations assume the passive is fully active at the start of the rotation. Yinlin's signature Rectifier is famous for its wide-spread use among all Rectifier damage dealers, Encore included. Thanks to its super high amount of CRIT Rate and generic damage boost on top of an easily activated ATK% boost, it stands above all other Rectifiers as the overall best weapon in the game.

example_teams.team_notes: If using Brant, put him in the second slot buffed by Lupa and have him buff Encore.

cons: Any non-modern DPS is powercrept, and she is no exception - her best teams only barely clear harder endgame content, and you need to put effort into your playstyle, with at least some basic Quickswap, to make it happen;

Main Echo is very awkward to use and essentially requires Quickswap with correct timing. Base Skill and its finisher attack work the same - in fact, since her Ultimate window is short and requires you to fit as many attacks as you can within it, her damage can vary wildly based on optimization.
pros: One of the best DPS that you can get without any limited banner pulls;
Lots of room for damage optimization, and Dodge Counters tend to be very beneficial;
Very accessible teammates, with room for upgrades via Mono Fusion.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Encore is a 5-star Fusion Rectifier DPS who was one of the earliest meta units in the game, as she was the best permanent banner DPS. As a matter of fact, this still holds true today, and while Encore does not get results that are up to par with the rest of the current meta, she can still provide decent results when played correctly.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Encore is one of very few characters whose Forte Circuit is not the focus of her kit. The highlight of Encore's kit, by a long shot, is her Ultimate. It sends her into the Cosmos Rave state for 10s, during which she unlocks a new Skill and new Basic Attacks that deal much higher damage than her base form. Dealing the highest damage that you can during this stance is her rotation goal. Typically, that's a mix of 3 Basic 4's (full attack strings) and 2 Skills, however one more Basic 4 can situationally be cast via her Dodge Counter, which behaves the exact same as her Basic 3, comboing into a much quicker Basic 4.

Her Forte is still used at the end of her Ultimate rotation though. It deals a good amount of damage over a long amount of time, increased if cast during her Ultimate stance (which is why we cast it at the very end), but it can (and must) be Swap Cancelled to compensate for this flaw. It's worth noting Encore has extremely high Forte gauge buildup, so practically no matter how unoptimized her rotation is, she'll always be able to cast it.

Her base form's Skill lasts a bit over a second. Encore shoots a barrage of 8 projectiles at one enemy and then can finish it off with a special Basic Attack, in total dealing quite a large amount of damage, but taking an extensive amount of time. Swap Cancelling a full cast of this Skill is another one of her rotation goals in Quickswap. However, requiring more Swaps than a standard rotation to execute, it's generally not considered for the majority of players. Still, it's an easy way to optimize Encore's damage. However, even in baseline rotations, it can be utilized as an easy way to trigger 5P Molten Rift's Set bonus and one of her Passives for a lot of extra Fusion DMG Bonus, by instantly interrupting it with her Ultimate after Intro.
Encore's passives give her 10% DMG Bonus each when she is above 70% HP (during her Ultimate) and when she casts any Resonance Skill (for 10s).
Lastly, her Intro and Outro are simple bursts of damage, nothing special there.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Encore was a staple of the meta on the game's initial release, however since then the damage ceiling of modern-day damage dealers raised significantly, making Encore pale in comparison to them. She nowadays struggles to clear the most challenging endgame content due to HP inflation.

However, that doesn't take away from her strengths: she's permanently accessible via the standard banner, and her weapon and buffing options are also always the generalist types. That means she accesses most of her damage potential with any limited banner weapon (or even the permanent Cosmic Ripples) and either Sanhua as a F2P buffer to hone in on her most important damage type (Basic Attack damage), or Lupa as a premium buffer to maximize her Fusion damage overall.

Nonetheless, upgrading to a team like Encore Brant Lupa or Encore Lupa Denia does not lead to a significant enough increase in Encore's damage ceiling to make her meta-relevant. Overall, you're simply better off pulling a premium DPS than upgrading Encore's own teammates. Generally, she'll be ran in a F2P team with Sanhua and Verina for example. That's not a bad thing though; given proper optimization, she can still clear some of the lower Tower of Adversity floors and even Endstate Matrix (leaning into Encore and Sanhua's 16s Ultimate cooldowns is particularly helpful for this).

In conclusion, while Encore's damage potential pales in comparison to modern damage dealers, she can still put in some work for a fully F2P DPS. She does not require a single limited banner pull to pick up and play in a decent team, and while that team is not up to par with the rest of the meta anymore, it can still get some results given the right amount of optimization, which is respectable compared to other permanent banner DPS choices.

synergies.commentary: Lupa is Encore's new best teammate over Sanhua in most situations. Lupa offers higher Fusion DMG-related buffs particularly with her Signature Weapon is equipped, and she provides an extra 7% DMG Amplification. While on paper this doesn't seem like much, Lupa also doubles if not triples Sanhua's damage output and fills in for downtimes that Encore typically experiences with Sanhua as they tend to rotate too quickly for their third teammate to keep up (Shorekeeper is a good example of this). This makes Lupa and Encore amazing partners.

One of Encore's strongest teammates by a lot. Super short field time and amazing 38% Basic Attack DMG Amplify on Outro, all the while providing strong buffs via her potential S6 and Echo Set, as well as complementing each other's few swap cancel windows perfectly (while far from necessary). Only comes at the cost of having low personal damage, but that's barely an inconvenience most of the time.

Complicated synergy, but Encore benefits from one of her Outro buffs (20% Fusion DMG) and they're both able to deal good damage on their own. Harder to play than Sanhua and overall less rewarding, but good nonetheless.

Similarly to Changli, Brant is a good option to consider for Dual DPS teams with Encore. Unlike Changli's Liberation DMG Amplify Outro Buff, Encore can utilize Brant's Skill DMG Amplify Outro buff on top of his general Fusion DMG Amplify, which makes the pair even stronger than the Changli version, also thanks to Brant's amazing personal damage.

These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Encore and Lupa because she enables Encore to work in a Hypercarry team while still sporting Lupa's full Mono Fusion buffs which makes her the best choice if that's available. Otherwise, Shorekeeper is amazing thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available..
